subject: Proposal: auto-renew clawback & notice alignment for ACME MSA
messages:
From: Luke Brennan <luke.brennan@acme.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme.com>
Date: 2027-07-25 09:12 -0700
Subject: Draft MSA term mechanics — auto-renew / notice / T4C

Sergio,

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. We've reviewed the draft MSA and have a few narrow asks on term mechanics we want to resolve before procurement signs off. High level: 1) ACME needs a fixed notice window that can't be shortened in an order form, 2) we want an auto-renew clawback for any unused committed credits if we give notice within the final 30 days, and 3) a clearer T4C (termination for convenience) remedy that includes a short transition assistance SLA and pro-rated refund for pre-paid capacity.

I've attached a redline with in-line comments (ACME_MSA_redline_2027.docx) and the latest order form (OrderForm_v3.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 60-day irrevocable notice minimum and the proposed clawback language, or suggest alternate fallback language for our legal team?

We'd like to avoid multi-week legal back-and-forth — if you can give a firm position by end of day Tuesday (27th) we can escalate internally.

Thanks,
Luke Brennan
Principal Procurement Manager — ACME Corporation
Attachment(s): ACME_MSA_redline_2027.docx (docx), OrderForm_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-25 10:08 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft MSA term mechanics — auto-renew / notice / T4C

Marissa / Naomi / Kim — forwarding ACME's asks on notice window, auto-renew clawback, and T4C transition support. Key points: ACME wants a 60-day irrevocable notice (instead of our standard 30), a clawback that returns unused committed credits if they give notice in final 30 days, and a concrete transition assistance commitment with a pro-rated refund under T4C.

My read:
- Notice window: customer asks for 60-day irrevocable minimum. We typically keep 30; 60 increases revenue tail risk but is reasonable if paired with stricter auto-renew opt-in language.
- Clawback: this is unusual — giving back unused committed credits on notice undermines committed revenue. Could consider limiting clawback to pilots <= $50k or to credits above an annualized floor.
- T4C: we can offer a 30-day transition assistance (knowledge transfer + limited support) and pro-rate any pre-paid, unused Dedicated capacity. But legal will push for 'best-efforts' vs SLA; sales should decide how firm to be.

Asking legal + pricing:
1) Marissa — can legal accept a 60-day notice but preserve that order forms cannot shorten it? If yes, any standard language you prefer?
2) Naomi — pricing: what's a simple clawback/floor we can offer that doesn't blow committed revenue forecasts? Suggestion: clawback limited to prepaid credits above 50% of annual commit, and only for customers with < $200k ARR in first year.
3) Kim — ops/CS: can we commit to 30 days of transition assistance with 8x5 email support and a single on-site (if requested at cost)?

Let's get a consolidated position to send to Luke by EOD Tuesday. If Legal needs a call with ACME counsel, we should schedule for Wednesday.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): forwarded ACME redline

From: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Luke Brennan <luke.brennan@acme.com>
Date: 2027-07-27 14:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA term mechanics — auto-renew / notice / T4C

Sergio — appreciate the quick turnaround and for looping in pricing/legal. A couple clarifications from our side after internal review: 1) the 60-day minimum is non-negotiable for ACME execs given vendor consolidation timelines, but we are open to tradeoffs (e.g., longer notice / reduced clawback scope). 2) on clawback we proposed returning unused committed credits only if notice is provided within the 30-day final window — we will accept a floor, but it needs to be meaningful (not just symbolic). 3) transition assistance: ACME needs a written commitment for 30 days of handoff with documented KPIs (response times, escalation path).

If Redwood can accept: (a) 60-day notice in the MSA with an explicit statement that order forms may not shorten the notice; (b) clawback capped at credits exceeding 40% of annual commit and limited to customers under $300k ARR in their first contract year; and (c) 30-day transition assistance with a measurable SLA (24 business-hour email response, one named technical lead, runbook delivery within 10 days), we can move to procurement signature next week and route the MSA to legal for final signoff.

We're attaching the annotated redline with the ACME execs' priorities highlighted for easy review. If you prefer to discuss one quick call Thursday morning, Beth and I can join.

Best,
Beth Carter
Head of Vendor Governance — ACME Corporation
Attachment(s): ACME_MSA_redline_2027.docx (annotated)
